item.title: Burnley Council Councillor Pay Rise vs Lancashire County Council Allowance Freeze: The Full Picture
item.description: Reform UK led a unanimous vote at Lancashire County Council to freeze all councillor allowances, saving up to £115,000. At Burnley Borough Council, Labour voted for pay increases in 2023 and 2024. Cllr Tom Pickup challenged Cllr Mark Townsend's incorrect Facebook claim that Reform were set to give themselves a pay rise.

item.title: Burnley Council Elections Cancelled: Labour Government Postpones Local Democracy Despite Scrutiny Committee Objection
item.description: The Labour Government cancelled Burnley Borough Council's May 2026 elections as part of a nationwide postponement affecting 30 councils, 19 of them Labour-run. Burnley's own Scrutiny Committee recommended proceeding with the vote, but the Executive overruled them. Reform UK's subsequent High Court legal challenge forced a government U-turn, and all elections were reinstated.

item.title: Burnley Council Budget 2026/27: £2.2 Million Business Rates Hit and What It Means for Council Tax
item.description: Burnley Borough Council faces its most challenging budget in years as a government business rates reset strips £2.2 million from income. With 67-70% of district councils expected to see real-terms funding fall, the 2026/27 budget will test whether Burnley can maintain its below-maximum council tax approach.

item.title: Burnley Council's Five-Unitary Gamble: Spending Taxpayer Money to Keep Themselves in a Job
item.description: Burnley Council is spending tens of thousands on consultants to push a five-unitary model for Lancashire — despite the strong case for fewer, larger authorities that would deliver real savings for residents.

item.title: East Lancashire's Waste Crisis: A Decade of Inaction, and the Councils Who Caused It
item.description: For years, Burnley, Pendle, Hyndburn and Rossendale failed to provide a waste transfer station. Reform inherited the mess in May 2025 — and the parties who caused it are now politicising the solution.

item.title: £5.3 Million Spent on Insurance and Brokerage
item.description: Council insurance costs have reached £5.3 million since 2021, with one insurance broker receiving £3.7 million in fees and premiums.

item.title: County Councillor Calls for Borough Councillor Resignations to Trigger By-Elections
item.description: County Councillor Tom Pickup called on Borough Councillors whose terms were due for re-election to resign, which would have triggered by-elections and given residents a democratic vote.

item.title: DOGE Analysis: £2.5M in Duplicate Payments, £10.5M Without Contracts, and Netflix on the Council Card
item.description: Our comprehensive DOGE-style audit of 19,865 spending records totalling £217 million has uncovered duplicate payments, suppliers operating without contracts, and questionable purchase card spending including Domino's Pizza and ChatGPT subscriptions.

item.title: £2.5 Million in Duplicate Payments Found in Council's Own Published Data
item.description: DOGE analysis confirms 1,284 exact duplicate records originating from the council's own CSV files — these are not our errors, they are theirs.

item.title: One Law Firm, One Day, £19.8 Million: The Geldards Question
item.description: A single capital programme payment of £19,848,934 to solicitors Geldards on 19 October 2021 — for the Pioneer Place development — exceeds the council's entire annual revenue budget.

item.title: £10.5 Million Paid to Suppliers With No Published Contract
item.description: Nine of the council's top 100 suppliers — receiving over £10.5 million between them — do not appear in the published contracts register.

item.title: ChatGPT, Aldi, and Oswaldtwistle Mill: What's on the Council Credit Cards?
item.description: Purchase card analysis reveals £1,397 on ChatGPT, £2,498 at Aldi on the Chief Executive's card, Domino's Pizza, Uber, and Just Eat — all charged to the taxpayer.

item.title: The £34 Million Liberata Deal: Outsourcing That Cut 40% of Jobs
item.description: Burnley's decade-long outsourcing contract with Liberata UK saw 40% of affected staff lose their jobs. Now the council is bringing services back in-house — was it worth it?

item.title: Council Cards Used for 51 Netflix Payments
item.description: Analysis reveals ongoing Netflix subscription payments on council purchase cards since 2021, raising questions about appropriate use of public funds.
